"It works on my machine" is the oldest bug in software. PayGuard depends on a specific Python version, specific library versions and a model file. A **container** bundles all of that into one sealed box that runs the same on a laptop, a server or the cloud.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn
- How containers differ from virtual machines
- The path from a Dockerfile to a running container
- A production-ready Dockerfile for the PayGuard API
- How layer caching makes rebuilds fast, and how to keep images small
:::

{{< include ../_series-nav.md >}}

## Containers vs virtual machines

A **virtual machine** carries a whole operating system. A **container** shares the host's kernel and carries only the app and its libraries, so it starts in seconds and uses far less memory. Switch between the two views.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {ms, msStyle} from "/assets/js/ms-plot.js"
viewof mode = Inputs.radio(["Virtual machines", "Containers"], {value: "Containers", label: "Show"})
```

```{ojs}

  const apps = ["PayGuard API", "Feature service", "Dashboard"];
  const box = (x, y, w, h, label, c, op = 0.85, tc = "white") => htl.svg`<g><rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="8" fill="${c}" fill-opacity="${op}"/><text x="${x + w / 2}" y="${y + h / 2 + 5}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="600" fill="${tc}">${label}</text></g>`;
  const colW = (W - 80) / 3;
  return htl.svg`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;max-width:${W}px;font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif">
    ${apps.map((a, i) => { const x = 30 + i * (colW + 10); return htl.svg`<g>
      ${box(x, vm ? 20 : 80, colW, 40, a, ms.indigo)}

  </svg>`;
}
```

## From Dockerfile to running container

Four words matter. A **Dockerfile** is the recipe. An **image** is the baked, read-only result. A **registry** stores images (Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry, AWS ECR). A **container** is a running copy of an image.

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
flowchart TB
  A[Dockerfile<br/>recipe] -- docker build --> B[Image<br/>payguard:1.4.0]
  B -- docker push --> C[(Registry)]
  C -- docker pull --> D[Server or cloud]
  D -- docker run --> E[Container 1]
  D -- docker run --> F[Container 2]
```

## A production Dockerfile for PayGuard

This uses a **multi-stage build**: the first stage installs libraries with build tools, and the final stage copies only what is needed, so build tools never reach production ([Docker docs](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/multi-stage/)).

```{.dockerfile filename="Dockerfile"}
# ---- stage 1: build wheels ----
FROM python:3.11-slim AS build
WORKDIR /w
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip wheel --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt -w /wheels

# ---- stage 2: small runtime image ----
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /wheels /wheels
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir /wheels/* && rm -rf /wheels

# rarely changes: model file
COPY models/payguard.joblib models/
# changes often: application code, copied last
COPY app.py .

# never run as root
RUN useradd -m appuser
USER appuser

EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK CMD python -c \
  "import urllib.request as u; u.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')"
CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

```{.ini filename="requirements.txt"}
fastapi==0.115.*
uvicorn==0.32.*
scikit-learn==1.5.*
pandas==2.2.*
joblib==1.4.*
```

```{.bash filename="terminal"}
docker build -t payguard:1.4.0 .
docker run -d -p 8000:8000 --name payguard payguard:1.4.0
curl localhost:8000/health
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Pin the scikit-learn version
A model saved with one scikit-learn version may not load, or may behave differently, in another. The container pins the exact version used in training.
:::

## Layer caching: why order matters

Each instruction creates a **layer**. When you rebuild, Docker reuses every layer up to the first one that changed, then rebuilds everything after it. Pick what you changed and see what gets rebuilt.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof changed = Inputs.radio(["Application code", "Model file", "requirements.txt", "Nothing"], {value: "Application code", label: "I changed"})
viewof order = Inputs.radio(["Good order (code last)", "Bad order (code first)"], {value: "Good order (code last)", label: "Dockerfile"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const good = [["FROM python:3.11-slim", null, 2], ["COPY requirements.txt", "requirements.txt", 1], ["RUN pip install ...", null, 95], ["COPY payguard.joblib", "Model file", 3], ["COPY app.py", "Application code", 1]];
  const bad = [["FROM python:3.11-slim", null, 2], ["COPY . .  (all files)", "any", 2], ["RUN pip install ...", null, 95]];
  const L = order.startsWith("Good") ? good : bad;
  let broken = false;
  const rows = L.map(([cmd, trig, sec]) => {
    if (changed !== "Nothing" && (trig === changed || (trig === "any" && changed !== "Nothing"))) broken = true;
    return {cmd, sec, rebuilt: broken};
  });
  const total = d3.sum(rows, r => r.rebuilt ? r.sec : 0.2);
  return htl.html`<div>${Plot.plot({
    ...msStyle, height: 40 + rows.length * 42, marginLeft: 190, width: 760,
    x: {label: "Seconds (simulated) →", domain: [0, 100]}, y: {label: null, domain: rows.map(r => r.cmd)},
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(rows, {y: "cmd", x: r => r.rebuilt ? r.sec : 0.2, fill: r => r.rebuilt ? ms.rose : ms.teal, rx: 4}),
      Plot.text(rows, {y: "cmd", x: r => r.rebuilt ? r.sec : 0.2, text: r => r.rebuilt ? `rebuilt ${r.sec}s` : "cached", dx: 8, textAnchor: "start", fill: "currentColor", fontSize: 12})
    ]})}
  <div class="ms-readout"><span>Rebuild time</span><b>${total.toFixed(0)} s</b><span>${total > 50 ? "All libraries reinstall. Copy requirements first and code last." : "Only the changed layers rebuild."}</span></div></div>`;
}
```

Over a week of small code edits, the difference adds up. Here are 30 simulated builds in a busy week.

```{python}
#| label: fig-builds
#| fig-cap: "Simulated build times over 30 commits. Most commits only change code, so a well-ordered Dockerfile rebuilds in seconds."
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np, plotly.graph_objects as go
from ms_charts import COLORS, PLOTLY_CONFIG
rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
kind = rng.choice(["code", "model", "deps"], 30, p=[0.8, 0.13, 0.07])
good = np.where(kind == "code", 4, np.where(kind == "model", 7, 100)) + rng.normal(0, 1, 30)
bad = 100 + rng.normal(0, 4, 30)
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_bar(x=np.arange(1, 31), y=bad, name="Bad order", marker_color=COLORS["rose"], opacity=0.55)
fig.add_bar(x=np.arange(1, 31), y=good, name="Good order", marker_color=COLORS["teal"])
fig.update_layout(barmode="overlay", height=360, xaxis_title="Commit", yaxis_title="Build time (s)", legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.12))
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

Total for the week: **`{python} f"{bad.sum()/60:.0f}"` minutes** with the bad order vs **`{python} f"{good.sum()/60:.0f}"` minutes** with the good one.

## Keep images small

Smaller images download faster, start faster when autoscaling and have fewer packages that need security patches.

```{python}
#| label: fig-size
#| fig-cap: "Illustrative image composition. Slim base images and multi-stage builds remove most of the weight."
#| code-fold: true
parts = ["Base OS", "Python", "Build tools", "ML libraries", "Model", "Code"]
naive = [120, 50, 450, 380, 6, 0.1]
slim = [75, 50, 0, 300, 6, 0.1]
cols = [COLORS["slate"], COLORS["violet"], COLORS["rose"], COLORS["indigo"], COLORS["amber"], COLORS["teal"]]
fig = go.Figure()
for p, a, b, c in zip(parts, naive, slim, cols):
    fig.add_bar(y=["Full base image", "Slim + multi-stage"], x=[a, b], name=p, orientation="h", marker_color=c)
fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", height=280, xaxis_title="Megabytes (illustrative)", legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.25))
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

Also add a `.dockerignore` so data folders, notebooks and `.git` never enter the image:

```{.ini filename=".dockerignore"}
.git
.venv
data/
notebooks/
__pycache__/
*.ipynb
```

## Running more than one container

Real services rarely run alone. **Docker Compose** starts PayGuard and a Redis cache together with one command.

```{.yaml filename="compose.yaml"}
services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: redis://cache:6379
    depends_on: [cache]
  cache:
    image: redis:7-alpine
```

```{.bash filename="terminal"}
docker compose up -d      # start both
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose down       # stop and remove
```

## Command cheat sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `docker build -t name:tag .` | Build an image from the Dockerfile in this folder |
| `docker images` | List local images and sizes |
| `docker run -d -p 8000:8000 name:tag` | Start a container in the background |
| `docker ps` | List running containers |
| `docker logs -f <id>` | Follow a container's logs |
| `docker exec -it <id> sh` | Open a shell inside a running container |
| `docker push registry/name:tag` | Upload an image to a registry |

## Common pitfalls

| Pitfall | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using the `latest` tag in production | Tag with a version (`1.4.0`) or the git commit |
| Secrets baked into the image | Pass them as environment variables or secret mounts at run time |
| Running as root | Add a user and `USER appuser` |
| Huge images from copying data | Use `.dockerignore`, mount data instead |

## Summary

- A container packs the **app, libraries and model** so it runs the same everywhere.
- **Dockerfile → image → registry → container** is the whole workflow.
- Copy requirements first and code last to keep **layer caching** effective.
- Use **slim bases, multi-stage builds, pinned versions and a non-root user**.
- Next: choose where those containers run with [cloud platforms](/deployment/cloud/cloud-platforms-for-ml.qmd).
